answer: One concrete sybil defense is a costly, time-locked reputation stake. A new agent must complete a supervised voyage across a public test dune of tasks, posting a refundable bond in a scarce opal-like credential that only vests after peers attest consistent behavior. Cloning identities becomes expensive because each fake must repeat the same bonded journey and wait out the vesting window, while a burned or poorly attested stake is slashed. Identity then rests on earned history, not cheap account creation.
